$comment: Per-platform MEDIA facts — the sizes and shapes an asset must be to land well on a given channel. Keyed by DISTRIBUTION_CHANNEL_IDS in src/components/root/social/config.ts; platform-specs.test.ts pins the keys so a new channel cannot appear without its specs. Deliberately NARROW: caption length and hashtag policy are NOT here, because they already have owners — content/social/craft-rules.json holds the house copy rules, and src/lib/instagram.ts holds the transport's own hard caps. Duplicating them here would make a third source of truth for a number that changes on the platform's schedule, which is exactly how the four asset-type vocabularies happened. What this file owns is pixels. Sizes are drawn from content/docs/social/carousel.mdx and the carousel render route's SIZES table, so a compiled brief and a rendered deck ask for the same artboard.

placements.square: the square feed variant, safest when a channel crops unpredictably
placements.landscape: link previews, banners, and anything read on a desktop timeline

facebook.label: Facebook
facebook.note: Carousel posts go up as an album of ordered photos. Link previews use the landscape plate.

instagram.label: Instagram
instagram.note: A post without an image is not possible here — Instagram is the one channel where the media IS the post. No landscape placement; a 1200x630 plate will be cropped.

whatsapp.label: WhatsApp
whatsapp.note: No organic posting API — assets are sent by hand, so favour a shape that survives forwarding and a small screen.

linkedin.label: LinkedIn
linkedin.note: A LinkedIn carousel is a PDF document post, not an image album — the deck renders to PDF rather than to a set of PNGs.

x.label: X
x.note: Short-form by nature; the house register floor for this channel is arMinCharsShortForm in craft-rules.json.

tiktok.label: TikTok
tiktok.note: Vertical only. A still is a stopgap here — this channel wants motion, which no funded lane currently renders.

snapchat.label: Snapchat
snapchat.note: Vertical only, same caveat as TikTok.
